lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Sharing ideas makes the light brighter! Today, we follow the bright beam from the lighthouse. We walk on a long glass bridge over the clouds. At the end of the bridge, there is a shining city. Tall towers have gardens on their roofs. Trees on the streets look like big solar panels. The air is clean and fresh. Look up! Cars are flying in the sky! Look down! Robots are working on the streets. Kiko says, Wow! Cars fly and robots work here. Say it with me. Cars fly and robots work here. Great job! Then a small round robot floats toward us. She is silver, and her eyes shine blue. She says, Beep! Welcome to the City of Tomorrow! Her name is Nova. She is our guide. Nova gives each of us a card. Let's read it. "Expo Pass. Welcome to the City of Tomorrow! This pass is for our special guests. In thirty days, we will have the World 30 Invention Expo in the city square. On your pass, there are six empty star badges. Learn about our city, our jobs, and our ideas, and your badges will light up. When all six badges shine, you can show your own invention at the Expo. Have fun, and ask lots of questions! From Nova, City Guide." How many star badges are there? Six. Where is the Expo? In the city square. Haru points at the sky. What's that? Nova answers, It's a flying car! Now, phonics. Today's word part is auto. Auto means self. Automatic. It works by itself. Autograph. You write your own name. Automobile. A car. It moves by itself. Autopilot. A plane can fly by itself. Let's explore the City of Tomorrow with Nova!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Cars fly and robots work here. Today, we walk down Main Street with Nova. The street is very clean. There is no trash anywhere. Why? Look! A small green robot is rolling along the sidewalk. It has two soft brushes and a long arm. Nova says, This is a robot that cleans the streets. A robot that cleans（そうじする ロボット）. Say it with me. This is a robot that cleans the streets. Very good! The robot picks up a can. Then it picks up a paper cup. It picks up trash and sorts it. Cans go in one box, and paper goes in another box. Riko asks, What does it do at night? Nova says, It cleans the streets at night, too. It never sleeps! Let's read the sign on the robot. "Hello! I am Street Helper Number Seven. I clean Main Street every day and every night. I pick up cans, bottles, and paper. I sort them, and then I take them to the recycling center. Please put your trash in the trash cans. That makes my job easier. If you see me, please step aside. I move slowly, so I am safe for people and pets. Thank you for keeping our city clean!" Where does the robot take the trash? To the recycling center. Is the robot safe for pets? Yes, because it moves slowly. The sign says, I move slowly. Is that a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Now, phonics. Auto means self. Autobiography. A book about your own life. You write it yourself. Automate. To make a machine do a job by itself. Automation. Machines doing jobs by themselves. Autocorrect. It fixes your spelling by itself. Let's keep the City of Tomorrow clean!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This is a robot that cleans the streets. Today, Nova takes us to a bus stop. A round white bus comes quietly. The door opens. We get on, but wait! There's no driver. Birimo says, Where is the driver? Nova laughs. Beep! There's no driver. It drives itself. We sit down and fasten our seat belts. The bus starts to move. Kiko says, We're riding a bus that drives itself. Say it with me. We're riding a bus that drives itself. Excellent! The bus moves slowly and carefully. Suddenly, a cat walks into the street. The bus stops at once. The cat looks at the bus and walks away. Everyone claps. Haru asks, Where does this bus go? Nova answers, It goes to the Sun Tower. Let's read the card on the wall. "Welcome aboard the Sky Line Bus. This bus drives itself. It has cameras on all sides, so it can see people, bikes, and animals. It always stops at red lights, and it never drives fast. Please fasten your seat belt. Press the blue button before your stop. If you need help, talk to the screen at the front. Next stops: Main Street, Solar Tree Park, the Sun Tower. Enjoy your ride, and please be kind to other passengers!" What does the bus have on all sides? Cameras. What should you press before your stop? The blue button. Riko says, I think this bus is safe because it never drives fast. Now, phonics. Auto means self. Autosave. The computer saves your work by itself. Autofocus. A camera makes the picture clear by itself. Autoplay. The next video starts by itself. Next stop, the Sun Tower!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, We're riding a bus that drives itself. Today, the bus stops in front of a very tall tower. It shines in the sunlight. Its walls are covered with solar panels. On the roof, small wind turbines are spinning. This is the Sun Tower. Nova says, That building makes its own energy. Say it with me. That building makes its own energy. Wonderful! Nova explains, It's a building which makes energy from the sun. It makes energy from the wind, too. Haru asks, Where does the extra energy go? Nova says, It goes to the houses. We ride the elevator to the top floor. There is a big screen with numbers on it. Let's read the information board. "The Sun Tower. This tower has two thousand solar panels and twelve small wind turbines. On sunny days, the panels change sunlight into electricity. On windy days, the turbines help, too. The tower uses this energy for its lights, elevators, and computers. When it makes more energy than it needs, the extra energy goes to houses nearby. Today, the tower is giving energy to three hundred homes. The Sun Tower makes no smoke, so the air stays clean." How many solar panels does the tower have? Two thousand. How many homes get energy today? Three hundred. Kiko says, I think this tower is amazing because the air stays clean. Is that a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Now, phonics. Auto means self. Automatically. The lights turn on automatically. They turn on by themselves. Autonomous. A machine is autonomous when it can decide and move by itself. Automaton. An old machine that moves like a person, like a dancing doll. Let's say thank you to the sun!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, That building makes its own energy. Today, we have an important job. A group of little ducklings is visiting the city with their teacher, Mrs. Waddle. Nova asks, Can you be their tour guides? Of course! Riko holds up a yellow flag. She says, Please follow me. We walk past Street Helper Number Seven and the Sun Tower. Then we arrive at a green park. Here we are! Kiko says, This is a park that has solar trees. Say it with me. This is a park that has solar trees. Perfect! The solar trees are tall, and their leaves are solar panels. Haru asks, Do you have any questions? A duckling says, Yes! What do the solar trees do? Haru reads the sign. "Solar Tree Park. Our solar trees are not real trees, but they work hard! Their leaves are solar panels. They give shade on hot days, so you can rest under them. They also make electricity from sunlight. You can charge bikes and scooters at the bottom of each tree. At night, the trees use the energy to light the paths. There are also real trees in the park, with birds and flowers. Enjoy both kinds of trees!" What can you charge at the bottom of each tree? Bikes and scooters. What do the trees do at night? They light the paths. The ducklings say, Thank you, guides! Then they ask for our autographs. Look at your Expo Pass. Beep! The first star badge is shining! Now, phonics. Let's review auto. Auto means self. Automatic. Autograph. Autopilot. Automation. Say auto clearly. Great job, tour guides!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This is a park that has solar trees. Today, Nova takes us on a job tour. We visit a bright studio full of colorful screens. A fox with round glasses waves at us. Her name is Ms. Lin. Nova says, She's a person who designs games. Say it with me. She's a person who designs games. Fantastic! Birimo is so excited. He loves games! Ms. Lin says, My job is to make games fun and fair. So Nova tells us, Her job is to make games fun and fair. Ms. Lin shows us her new game. Players help a little robot build a bridge. Kiko asks, How do you make a game? Ms. Lin shows us her planning board. Let's read it. "How I Design a Game. Step one: I think of an idea. My new game is about a robot that builds bridges. Step two: I draw the characters and the world. Step three: I test the game with children, and I listen to their opinions. Step four: I make it better. A good game is fun, but it is also fair. Everyone can win if they practice. My games also say, Time for a break, after thirty minutes. Our eyes and bodies need rest." What does Ms. Lin do in step three? She tests the game with children. What do her games say after thirty minutes? Time for a break! Riko says, I think that's a great idea because breaks are important. Now, phonics. Today's word part is trans. Trans means across or change. Transport. To carry things from one place to another. Transform. To change into something new. Translate. To change words into another language. Transfer. To move something to a different place. Let's thank Ms. Lin!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, She's a person who designs games. Today, our job tour continues. Nova takes us to the City Helper Center. There are many different jobs here. In the first room, we meet a doctor and a nurse. Nova says, Doctors are people who help sick people. Say it with me. Doctors are people who help sick people. Very nice! In the next room, there is a big red fire truck. Haru says, Firefighters are people who put out fires. In the last room, a woman is fixing a robot arm. She is a robot mechanic. Kiko asks, Who helps us when we're sick? Riko answers, Doctors and nurses do. On the wall, there is a big poster. Let's read it. "Thank You, City Helpers! Every day, many people help our city. Doctors and nurses help sick people get better. Firefighters put out fires and rescue people. Recycling workers collect cans and bottles, so we can use them again. Robot mechanics fix our street robots and buses. Robots can do many jobs, but they can't do everything. People are still very important! Next time you see a city helper, please say thank you." Who collects cans and bottles? Recycling workers. Who fixes the street robots? Robot mechanics. Birimo says, I think firefighters are the bravest people because they help people in danger. Is that a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Now, phonics. Trans means across or change. Transmit. To send a message or a signal across. Transplant. To move a plant to a new place. Transportation. Buses, trains, and cars. They carry people from place to place. Let's say thank you to our city helpers!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Doctors are people who help sick people. Today, we hear a happy bark. Woof! Woof! A shiny metal dog runs to us. It wags its silver tail. Then a girl with a big tool belt runs after it. Nova says, This is Tess. This is the girl who invented the robot dog. Say it with me. This is the girl who invented the robot dog. Great! Tess is eleven years old. Her robot dog's name is Sprocket. Riko asks, When did you make it? Tess says, I made it when I was ten. Haru asks, Was it easy? Tess laughs. No! I made many mistakes, but I didn't give up. Tess shows us her notebook. Let's read one page. "My Robot Dog Notebook. Try one: Sprocket's legs were too weak. He fell down. Try two: His battery was too small. He stopped after five minutes. Try three: He walked, but he walked backward! Try four: I changed his legs, his battery, and his program. He walked forward, he wagged his tail, and he barked! I learned something important. Mistakes are not bad. Mistakes help me learn. Now Sprocket is my best friend." How many tries did Tess need? Four. What did Sprocket do in try three? He walked backward. Kiko says, I think Tess is amazing because she never gave up. Do you agree? Now, phonics. Trans means across or change. Translation. Changing words into another language. Transformation. A big change, like a caterpillar into a butterfly. Transit. Moving people from place to place, like a city bus or a train. Let's never give up, just like Tess!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This is the girl who invented the robot dog. Today, Nova has a quiz for us. It's called Who Am I? Nova reads a hint, and we guess the job. Nova says, I'm a person who works at night and keeps you safe. Say it with me. I'm a person who works at night and keeps you safe. Excellent! Haru raises his hand. Are you a police officer? Nova says, That's right! It can be a night guard, too. Now it's Kiko's turn. She says, Give me one more hint, please. Let's read the quiz cards. "Quiz Card One: I'm a person who gets up very early. I make bread and cakes, and my shop smells wonderful. Quiz Card Two: I'm a person who grows rice and vegetables. I work outside in the sun and the rain. Quiz Card Three: I'm a person who works in space. I float in my ship, and I can see the whole Earth from my window. Quiz Card Four: I'm a robot that helps visitors. I can float, and my eyes shine blue." Who is Card One? A baker. Card Two? A farmer. Card Three? An astronaut. And Card Four? It's Nova! Everyone laughs. Riko says, I think an astronaut has the most exciting job because you can see the Earth from space. Is that a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Now, phonics. Trans means across or change. Translator. A person who changes words into another language. Transformer. A machine that changes electricity. Transmission. Sending a message or a signal through the air. Now you can make a Who Am I quiz, too!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'm a person who works at night and keeps you safe. Today, Nova takes us to the Future Job Fair. There are many booths with bright posters. Nova says, In the future, there will be people who take care of robots. Say it with me. In the future, there will be people who take care of robots. Wonderful! Tess is here, too, with Sprocket. She wants to be a robot caretaker when she grows up. Riko asks Haru, What do you want to be? Haru says, I want to be an ocean cleaner. Kiko says, I want to be a space farmer because I like plants. Let's read the big poster at the entrance. "Jobs of Tomorrow. Robot caretakers check robots every day and fix them when they break. Space farmers grow vegetables in gardens on the moon. Ocean cleaners use boats and drones to pick up plastic from the sea. Game designers make fun and fair games for everyone. Some of these jobs don't exist yet. Maybe you will invent a new job! What do you love? What are you good at? Your answers can help you find your future job." Who grows vegetables on the moon? Space farmers. What do ocean cleaners pick up? Plastic. Birimo says, I want to be a cake tester! Is that a real job? Maybe in the future! Everyone laughs. Look at your Expo Pass. The second star badge is shining! Now, phonics. Let's review trans and auto. Transport. Transform. Trans means across or change. Autocorrect. Autonomous. Auto means self. Say the first part clearly. See you at the next booth!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In the future, there will be people who take care of robots. Today, we walk up Hill Street with Tess and Sprocket. Hill Street is very steep. Halfway up the hill, we see an old tortoise. His name is Mr. Shell. He is carrying two big shopping bags, and he is walking very slowly. He puts the bags down and breathes hard. Kiko asks, What's the problem? Mr. Shell smiles and says, The hill is steep, and the bags are heavy. Tess opens her notebook. She says, Inventors always start with a problem. The problem is that older people can't carry heavy bags. Say it with me. The problem is that older people can't carry heavy bags. Great job! Haru carries one bag, and Riko carries the other one. Mr. Shell says, Thank you, but you can't help me every day. Tess nods and says, Let's find a way to help. Let's read a page from Tess's notebook. "Tess's Problem Notebook, Page 12. Today I watched Hill Street for one hour. Seven older people walked up the hill with shopping bags. Five of them stopped to rest three times or more. Mr. Shell stopped six times. His bags were full of apples, milk, and bread. He told me, The hill is not my problem. The bags are my problem. Big question for tomorrow: How can we make heavy bags easy to carry?" How many older people walked up the hill? Seven. How many times did Mr. Shell stop? Six times. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Tess counted carefully. Now, phonics. Today's word ending is ic. Listen carefully. Say the part just before ic strongly. Electric. LEC is strong. Robotic. BOT is strong. Scientific. TIF is strong. Fantastic. TAS is strong. Fantastic job! Next time, let's think of a great idea for Mr. Shell!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The problem is that older people can't carry heavy bags. Today, we go to Tess's lab. It is full of tools, wires, and old robot parts. Sprocket runs around and barks happily. Tess puts a big board on the wall. She says, This is our idea board. Every idea is welcome. I ask, Do you have any ideas? Haru says, How about a robot arm? Kiko says, How about a moving sidewalk on Hill Street? Birimo says, How about balloons? Then Riko stands up. She says, My idea is a bag that follows you. Say it with me. My idea is a bag that follows you. Wonderful! Tess claps her hands and says, That's a great idea! Let's draw it. Let's read the idea board. "Tess's Idea Board. Idea 1, from Haru: a robot arm that lifts heavy bags. It is strong, but it is very big. Idea 2, from Kiko: a moving sidewalk on Hill Street. It helps everyone, but it takes years to build. Idea 3, from Birimo: balloons that lift bags into the sky. It is fun, but windy days are dangerous. Idea 4, from Riko: a bag that follows you. It is small, and it can go anywhere." Whose idea is the moving sidewalk? It's Kiko's idea. Which idea can go anywhere? Riko's bag. The friends talk about every idea and give reasons. In the end, they choose Riko's idea. Small ideas can help a lot. Now, phonics. Remember, with words that end in ic, say the part just before ic strongly. Magnetic. NET is strong. Electronic. TRON is strong. Energetic. JET is strong. Futuristic. fu-tur-IS-tic. The City of Tomorrow looks so futuristic! Next time, let's find out how the bag works.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, My idea is a bag that follows you. Today, we design the bag. Tess gives us a big piece of paper and some colored pens. Haru asks, How does the bag know where Mr. Shell is? Nova floats over. Beep! She says, It uses sensors to find you. Say it with me. It uses sensors to find you. Great! Nova says, I use sensors, too. They help me see the street, and they help me stop before I hit a wall. Riko draws the bag. It has a small camera and four wheels. Kiko writes, When you walk, it moves. When you stop, it stops. Haru says, I think the wheels should be big because Hill Street is bumpy. Everyone agrees. Let's read our design card. "Design Card: The Follow-Me Bag. Size: as big as a backpack. Parts: four wheels, a small camera, two sensors, a battery, and a solar panel on the lid. How it works: First, you wear a small band on your wrist. The sensors look for the band. When you walk, the bag moves. When you stop, it stops. The battery charges in the sunshine, so you never need to plug it in." What is on the lid? A solar panel. What do the sensors look for? The band on your wrist. Is this a fact or an opinion? Well, it's a plan. We haven't tested it yet! Now, phonics. Let's say more ic words. Say the part just before ic strongly. Artistic. TIS is strong. Riko's drawing is very artistic. Athletic. LET is strong. Dramatic. MAT is strong. Terrific. RIF is strong. Terrific work today! Next time, we test the bag on Hill Street.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It uses sensors to find you. Today is test day! We take the Follow-Me Bag to Hill Street. Mr. Shell puts on the wrist band and starts to walk. The bag follows him. Hooray! But then a cat runs by. The bag turns and follows the cat into a garden! Then, at the stairs, the bag falls over. Oh no! Haru asks, What went wrong? Riko says, The camera saw the cat. Kiko says, And the wheels are too small for the stairs. Tess smiles. She says, Mistakes help me learn. We turn off the camera and put on bigger wheels. Tess says, It didn't work well, so we changed the design. Say it with me. It didn't work well, so we changed the design. Excellent! Then we say, Let's try again. Mr. Shell walks up the hill, and the bag follows him all the way. This time, it worked! Let's read Tess's test report. "Test Report: The Follow-Me Bag. Test 1, Monday. The bag followed Mr. Shell for ten meters. Then it saw a cat and followed the cat into a garden. At the stairs, it fell over. Changes: We turned off the camera, so now the bag follows only the wrist band. We put on bigger wheels and added a red stop button. Test 2, Tuesday. The bag climbed all the way up Hill Street. Mr. Shell did not stop even once!" What did the bag follow in the first test? A cat. What did they add? Bigger wheels and a red stop button. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Tess wrote down what really happened. Now, phonics. More ic words! Say the part just before ic strongly. Realistic. LIS is strong. Historic. TOR is strong. Organic. GAN is strong. Volcanic. CAN is strong. Fantastic testing, everyone! Next time, we show our invention to the judges.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It didn't work well, so we changed the design. Today is the Invention Pitch! Teams from all over the city come to Tess's lab. One team has a hat that plays music. Another team has shoes that light up at night. The judges are Nova and Ms. Lin. Our team is next. Riko stands up and says, Hello, judges! This is an invention that helps older people carry bags. Say it with me. This is an invention that helps older people carry bags. Wonderful! Haru says, Let me show you how it works. Mr. Shell walks, and the bag follows him. Kiko says, Thank you for listening. Do you have any questions? Let's read our pitch. "Hello, judges! This is the Follow-Me Bag. Here is the problem. Hill Street is steep, and shopping bags are heavy. Here is our idea. The bag uses sensors to find a band on your wrist, so it follows you everywhere. We tested it two times. The first test didn't work well, so we changed the design. Now it climbs the whole hill. Mr. Shell uses it every day. Thank you for listening!" How many times did they test the bag? Two times. Who uses it every day? Mr. Shell. Then Nova asks, What happens in the rain? Riko says, The bag is waterproof. The judges smile and give us the Best Helper Prize! Look at your Expo Pass. The third star badge is shining! Now, phonics. Let's review. Electric. Say LEC strongly. Fantastic. Say TAS strongly. Transmit. Trans means across. Transmit means send across. Autosave. Auto means self. The computer saves your work by itself. Great job, inventors! Next time, we talk about robots, their good points and their problems.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This is an invention that helps older people carry bags. Today, we visit the Robot Station. Many robots are resting and charging here. Kiko asks Nova, What are the good points of robots? Nova says, Beep! Robots can do hard jobs for you. We work at night, and we check bridges in the rain. Then Haru says, One good point is that robots never get tired. One problem is that they can break. Say it with me. One good point is that robots never get tired. One problem is that they can break. Very good! Nova nods. That's true. I need energy every day, and sometimes I need repairs. And I can't give you a warm hug like a friend. I ask, What do you think about robots? Let's read the big sign at the Robot Station. "Robots in the City of Tomorrow. There are about two thousand robots in our city. They clean streets, drive buses, and check bridges at night. Robots never get tired, and they can do jobs that are dangerous for people. But robots can break, and they need a lot of energy. They also cannot understand feelings the way friends do. That is why robots and people work together here. Robots do the heavy jobs, and people make the big decisions." How many robots are there in the city? About two thousand. Who makes the big decisions? People do. Is this sign mostly facts or opinions? It's mostly facts. Now, phonics. Today, we read short words made of capital letters. Say each letter clearly. AI. A, I. It means artificial intelligence. USB. U, S, B. TV. T, V. PC. P, C. Good job! Next time, let's talk about screens.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, One good point is that robots never get tired. One problem is that they can break. Today, we walk through the Sky Market. There are screens everywhere. There are screens on the walls, on the buses, and even on the tables! Birimo watches funny videos for a long time. Then he rubs his eyes. Kiko says, My eyes feel tired, too. Nova floats over. Beep! Screens are useful, but we need breaks. Say it with me. Screens are useful, but we need breaks. Nice! Haru asks, How much screen time is OK? Nova says, It's different for every family. Talk with your family and make a plan together. Then I say, Let's look far away and rest our eyes. We look at the clouds and the mountains far away. Ah, that feels much better. Let's read a poster from the City Health Center. "Screen Smart Tips. One: Every twenty minutes, look at something far away for twenty seconds. Two: Sit up straight, and keep the screen at arm's length. Three: Turn off screens one hour before bed. Your brain needs quiet time to sleep well. Four: Play outside every day. Sunlight and running are good for your body and your eyes. Screens are useful, but your eyes need breaks!" How often should you look far away? Every twenty minutes. When should you turn off screens? One hour before bed. Now, phonics. Some short words are units. We don't read the letters. We read the whole word. km. We say kilometers. cm. We say centimeters. kg. We say kilograms. mm. We say millimeters. The Sky Market is two kilometers long! Next time, we learn how to be safe online.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Screens are useful, but we need breaks. Today, we visit the City Library. Children in this city share pictures and stories on the Kids Board. Birimo takes a photo and says, I'm going to post it on the Kids Board! Post（とうこうする） means put something online for other people to see. Riko looks at the photo. Wait! I can see your house number in the photo. Haru says, Think before you post. Say it with me. Think before you post. Great! Haru adds, Don't share your address or school name online. Birimo says, Oops! I didn't think about that. I'll choose a different photo. Nova says, Beep! And if something feels wrong, tell a grown-up. Let's read the rules of the Kids Board. "Kids Board Rules. One: Think before you post. Once you post something, many people can see it, and it is hard to take back. Two: Never share your address, your phone number, or your school name. Three: Be kind. Write only things you would say to someone's face. Four: Some people online are not who they say they are. Never meet people from the internet. Five: If something feels wrong, tell a grown-up right away." What should you never share? Your address, your phone number, or your school name. Who should you tell when something feels wrong? A grown-up. Is rule three a fact or an opinion? It's a rule, and a very good one! Now, phonics. Some short words have numbers or letters. 3D. We say three D. It means you can see something from every side. VR. V, R. LED. L, E, D. Our classroom lights are LED lights. GPS. G, P, S. A GPS helps you find the way. Next time, we meet the AI Helper.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Think before you post. Today, we go back to the City Library. There is an AI Helper on a big screen. You can ask it questions. Kiko is doing her homework about spiders. She asks the AI Helper, How many legs do spiders have? The AI Helper says, Spiders have six legs. Haru asks, Is that answer right? Let's check it in a book. Riko opens a big book about insects and spiders. It says spiders have eight legs! Nova says, Beep! AI can make mistakes, too. Even I make mistakes sometimes. Kiko says, AI can help us, but we should check the answers. Say it with me. AI can help us, but we should check the answers. Well done! Let's read the sign next to the AI Helper. "How to Use the AI Helper. The AI Helper can answer questions, explain hard words, and give you ideas. It is fast and friendly. But sometimes it makes mistakes, and it can sound sure even when it is wrong. So check important answers in two places, like a book and a museum website. Ask a teacher or a librarian, too. Remember, the AI Helper can help you think, but your own thinking is the most important part." How many places should you check? Two places. Who else can you ask? A teacher or a librarian. Is it a fact that spiders have eight legs? Yes, it is. Now, phonics. Some short words are read as one word. NASA. We say NASA, not N, A, S, A. STEM. We say STEM. It means science, technology, engineering, and math. Other short words use letters. ID. I, D. DIY. D, I, Y. It means do it yourself. Next time, let's have a Technology Talk!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, AI can help us, but we should check the answers. Today is the Technology Talk in the city square. Robots, animals, and people sit together in a big circle. Riko leads the talk. She says, Today's topic is technology. What do you think about technology, Haru? Haru says, I think technology is helpful because it saves time. However, we shouldn't use it too much. Say it with me. I think technology is helpful because it saves time. However, we shouldn't use it too much. Excellent! Kiko agrees with Haru. Birimo says, I see your point, but I think playing outside is more fun than playing with robots. Riko smiles and says, Both sides have good reasons. Let's read Riko's notes. "Technology Talk Notes. Topic: Is technology good for us? Haru: Yes, because it saves time. The Follow-Me Bag helps Mr. Shell every day. Kiko: Yes, but we should take breaks from screens. Birimo: Robots are fun, but I still love playing outside with my friends. Riko: Technology can help us, but we should check answers and think for ourselves. Our group's idea: Technology is a great tool, and people should decide how to use it." Why does Haru think technology is helpful? Because it saves time. What does Birimo still love? Playing outside with his friends. Is the group's idea a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Look at your Expo Pass. The fourth star badge is shining! Now, phonics. Let's review. AI. A, I. 3D. Three D. Robotic. Say BOT strongly. Translator. Trans means across. A translator changes words into another language. Automate. Auto means self. Machines can automate hard jobs. Wonderful talk, everyone! Next time, we visit a museum of the future.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think technology is helpful because it saves time. However, we shouldn't use it too much. Today, Nova takes us to a new place. It's Tomorrow Hall, a museum of predictions. A prediction is a guess about the future. On the walls, there are big screens with pictures of the year 2050. Nova floats to the first screen and says, Beep! In 2050, people will probably live longer. Say it with me. In 2050, people will probably live longer. Excellent! Riko asks, Why do you think so? Nova answers, Because medicine will be better, and people will eat healthier food. Kiko asks, What will life be like in 2050? Haru says, I think we'll travel to the moon for vacation. Birimo says, I think robots will probably cook all my snacks! Let's read the card under the screen. "Prediction Number One. In 2050, people will probably live longer than today. Why? Doctors are learning more every year. New medicine can stop many illnesses early. Many people also exercise more and eat more vegetables. But nobody can see the future for sure. A prediction is not a fact. It is a smart guess with good reasons. What do you think? Write your own prediction on a paper star and stick it on the wall!" Is a prediction a fact? No, it's a smart guess. What do people eat more of? Vegetables. Doctors are learning more every year. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Now, phonics. Today, we listen to fast, friendly English. I'm gonna try it. Gonna means going to. We're gonna be late. I wanna see the robot. Wanna means want to. Do you wanna play? Friends talk like this, but when we write, we use going to and want to. Let's make a prediction star together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In 2050, people will probably live longer. Today, we visit the second room in Tomorrow Hall. It looks like a classroom, but there are no desks! There is a robot teacher with a friendly face, and a big window that shows a rainforest. Nova says, Beep! In the future, students might learn at home with robots. Say it with me. Students might learn at home with robots. Great! Kiko says, That might be fun, but I'd miss my friends. Haru asks, What will schools be like in the future? Riko answers, Maybe classes will be outside, in gardens and forests. Birimo says, Maybe lunch will be four hours long! Everyone laughs. Let's read the poster on the wall. "Schools in the Future: Three Ideas. Idea one: Students might learn at home with robot teachers. They can study at their own speed. Idea two: Classes might happen outside more often. Students can learn about plants by touching real plants. Idea three: Students might visit faraway places on screens and talk with children around the world. But one thing will not change. Friends and teachers help us learn and grow." What is idea two? Classes might happen outside more often. What will not change? Friends and teachers help us learn and grow. Students might learn at home. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a prediction, so it's not a fact yet. Now, phonics. Here is more fast, friendly English. You gotta see this. Gotta means got to. I gotta go now. It's kinda cool. Kinda means kind of. I'm kinda tired. We hear these words with friends, but we write got to and kind of. See you next time in Tomorrow Hall!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Students might learn at home with robots. Today, we enter the third room of Tomorrow Hall. It's a design studio! There is a big table with a magic drawing screen. Nova says, Beep! Please design your future home. Riko draws first. She says, My future home will have a garden on the roof. Say it with me. My future home will have a garden on the roof. Wonderful! Riko says, We can grow tomatoes and watch the stars up there. Haru says, It will have windows that make energy from the sun. Kiko asks, Birimo, what will your future home have? Birimo answers, It will have a slide from my bedroom to the kitchen! Nova says, That's creative! Let's read Riko's design card. "My Future Home, by Riko. My future home will have a garden on the roof. I will grow tomatoes, beans, and flowers there. Birds and bees will visit, too. The windows will make energy from sunlight, so the house will not need much power from outside. Rainwater will go into a big tank, and I will use it for the garden. My favorite room will be a quiet reading room with a round window." Where will Riko grow tomatoes? On the roof. Where will the rainwater go? Into a big tank. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's Riko's plan for the future. Now, phonics. Lemme try. Lemme means let me. Lemme see. Gimme a minute. Gimme means give me. Gimme five! That means give me a high five. These are friendly, fast words. In writing, we use let me and give me. Let's design our homes, everyone!

phonics.tipJa: dunno は don't know（しらない・わからない）、outta は out of（〜から 出て）を はやく いった かたち。かく ときは don't know・out of と かこう。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, My future home will have a garden on the roof. Today, we visit the energy room in Tomorrow Hall. There are two small model cities on a table. One city has smoke and gray air. The other city has wind turbines, solar panels, and blue skies. Nova says, Beep! Clean energy comes from the sun, the wind, and water. If we use clean energy, the air will be cleaner. Say it with me. If we use clean energy, the air will be cleaner. Very good! Haru asks, What will happen if we save energy, too? Nova answers, We'll need less power. Kiko turns off a light in the model city. Ding! A little green leaf lights up. Let's read the sign next to the models. "Energy from Nature. Sunlight, wind, and moving water never run out. We call this clean energy, because it makes very little smoke. If we use clean energy, the air will be cleaner and the sky will be bluer. Saving energy helps, too. Turn off lights you don't need. Close the fridge quickly. Walk or ride a bike for short trips. Small actions in many homes make a big difference for our planet." What are three kinds of clean energy? Sunlight, wind, and moving water. What can we do for short trips? Walk or ride a bike. Clean energy makes very little smoke. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Now, phonics. I dunno. Dunno means don't know. I dunno why. Let's get outta here. Outta means out of. Get outta the rain. We hear these words in fast talk with friends. When we write, we use don't know and out of. Let's save energy together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, If we use clean energy, the air will be cleaner. Today is presentation day in Tomorrow Hall! The friends made a big map of their own future city. Now they stand in front of everyone. Kiko starts. In our future city, there will be many parks and quiet buses. Say it with me. In our future city, there will be many parks and quiet buses. Wonderful! Haru gives a reason. One reason is that clean air is good for everyone. Riko adds, There will be a library which floats in the sky. Birimo says, There will be a giant cake shop, of course! Then he asks, Nova, what will there be in your future city? Nova answers, There will be benches and gentle hills for older people. Let's read their plan. "Our Future City Plan. In our future city, there will be many parks and quiet buses. The buses will run on clean energy. Every home will have a roof garden, and the streets will have solar trees for shade. There will be a sky library, a big sports field, and benches for older people. One problem is that it will cost a lot of money. So we will build the city little by little, together." What will the buses run on? Clean energy. What is one problem? It will cost a lot of money. Nova beeps happily. The fifth star badge on our Expo Passes is shining! Now, phonics. Let's review. I'm gonna try it. Gonna means going to. USB. We say U, S, B, one letter at a time. Futuristic. Say fu-tu-RIS-tic. Transport. Trans means across, so we carry things across. Automatic. Auto means self. Only one more badge to go!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In our future city, there will be many parks and quiet buses. Today, we visit Tess and Sprocket again. Tess is fixing a robot arm in her lab. She talks very fast. Tess says, I'm gonna try it! Haru looks confused. Gonna? What does that mean? Nova says, Beep! Gonna is a short way to say going to. Say it with me. "I'm gonna try it!" means "I'm going to try it." Great job! Then Tess asks, Do you wanna play a robot game? Riko answers, Sure! I'm gonna win! Let's read the note on the lab wall. "Fast Friend Talk, by Tess. When I talk with my friends, I often use short words. Gonna means going to. Wanna means want to. Gotta means got to. Kinda means kind of. We say these words with friends, but we write going to and want to. In a letter, a report, or a test, please use the full words. Then people all around the world can understand you. Sprocket only says woof, so he doesn't need this note!" What does wanna mean? Want to. When do we use the full words? In a letter, a report, or a test. Gonna means going to. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Birimo says, I'm gonna eat lunch now! Ha ha. Remember, gonna is fine with friends, but not in your notebook. Now, phonics. We're gonna be late. Do you wanna play? TV. We say T, V. Electric. Say e-LEC-tric. Transform. Trans means change, so transform means change shape. Autograph. Auto means self, so it's your own name. Have fun talking with your friends!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, "I'm gonna try it!" means "I'm going to try it." Today, Nova gives us the city newspaper, The Tomorrow Times. Let's read the top article together. "Tree Robot Helps Bald Mountain. Last spring, a small robot named Rooty went to work on Bald Mountain. Strong winds knocked down the trees there five years ago. Rooty can dig a hole, plant a seed, and give it water. It plants three hundred trees a day. It uses a camera to find good soil. Some people worry that robots will take people's jobs. But here, local children plant trees with Rooty every weekend. Now the mountain is turning green again." Kiko says, This article is about a robot that plants trees. Say it with me. This article is about a robot that plants trees. Excellent! Riko asks, What's the main idea? Haru answers, The main idea is that robots can help nature. Where did the robot plant the trees? It planted them on a mountain. How many trees does Rooty plant a day? Three hundred. Some people worry about jobs. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact that some people feel this way. Birimo says, I think Rooty is the best robot ever! That's an opinion. Good readers always find the main idea first. Then they carefully look for details, like numbers, names, and places. Now, phonics. You gotta see this. Gotta means got to. GPS. We say G, P, S. It helps us find places. Scientific. Say sci-en-TIF-ic. Transmission. Trans means across, so it sends something across. Automation. Auto means self. Keep reading, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This article is about a robot that plants trees. Today, we write invention proposals for the Expo. Tess says, A good proposal tells the name, what it does, how it works, who it helps, and one problem. Kiko has an idea. My invention is a pencil that checks spelling. It will help students write better. Say it with me. My invention is a pencil that checks spelling. It will help students write better. Super! Let's read Kiko's proposal. "Invention Proposal: The Spell Pencil. My invention is a pencil that checks spelling. It will help students write better. It has a tiny light that turns red when I make a mistake. A small computer inside the pencil knows many words. It does not fix the mistake for you. You think and fix it yourself, so you learn. One problem is that it might be expensive. We can use cheap parts and share the pencils in class." Who will the Spell Pencil help? Students. When does the light turn red? When you make a mistake. Why doesn't it fix mistakes? Because you learn more when you fix them yourself. Haru wants to make a shoe that cleans the floor. Birimo wants a lunch box that sings! Now it's your turn. Write about eighty words. Tell the name, the job, how it works, who it helps, and one problem. Now, phonics. It's kinda cool. Kinda means kind of. STEM. We say it like one word, STEM. It means science, technology, engineering, and math. Energetic. Say en-er-JET-ic. Translation. Trans means across, from one language to another. Autocorrect. Auto means self. Happy writing, inventors!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, My invention is a pencil that checks spelling. It will help students write better. Today, Nova takes us on a goodbye tour of the city. We ride the bus that drives itself. We wave to the street-cleaning robots and the Sun Tower. In Solar Tree Park, a little green robot is busy. Haru says, This is a robot that waters flowers. One good point is that it saves water. Say it with me. This is a robot that waters flowers. One good point is that it saves water. Perfect! We also visit our friends. Ms. Lin is a person who designs games. Tess is a girl who invents robots. Then Nova takes us to the city square. Under the square, there is an old stone stairway. At the bottom, there is a wooden door with a big clock on it. Kiko asks, What's behind that old door? Nova says, I'm not sure. It has been closed for a long time. Let's read the sign on the door. "This door opens to a very long hallway. Each room in the hallway shows a different time. Some rooms are full of old toys, old houses, and old roads. People built this city with ideas from the past. To open the door, bring an idea for the future. Then the clock will tick, and the heavy wooden door will slowly open for you." What is behind the door? A long hallway. When will the door open? When we bring an idea for the future. Now, phonics. Let's get outta here. Outta means out of. VR. We say V, R. Magnetic. Say mag-NET-ic. Transplant. Trans means across, so we move a plant to a new place. Automatic. Auto means self. Let's get ready for the Expo!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This is a robot that waters flowers. One good point is that it saves water. Today is the big day. It's the World 30 Invention Expo! It's also our nine hundredth lesson! The city square is full of tables and lights. Mr. Shell shows the Follow-Me Bag. Kiko shows the Spell Pencil. Haru shows his floor-cleaning shoe, and Birimo shows a lunch box that sings. Tess and Sprocket cheer for everyone. Nova says, Congratulations on nine hundred lessons! Then she says, The future is something that we create together. Say it with me. The future is something that we create together. Fantastic! Suddenly, the sixth star badge on our Expo Passes begins to shine. All six badges are shining! Let's read the Expo poster. "Welcome to the World 30 Invention Expo! Today, young inventors share ideas that help people and nature. Some inventions are big, and some are small. Some worked the first time, and some needed many tests. Every inventor asked good questions, listened to friends, and never gave up. Thank you for visiting the City of Tomorrow. The future is not something we just wait for. We build it together, one idea at a time." What did every inventor do? They asked good questions, listened to friends, and never gave up. Is this a fact or an opinion? The future is something we build together. It's an opinion, and a good one! Look! Under the square, the clock door is opening! Tick, tock! It's the Corridor of Time! Now, phonics. Gimme five! Gimme means give me. AI. We say A, I. Futuristic. Say fu-tu-RIS-tic. Transportation. Trans means across. Automaton. Auto means self. See you in the Corridor of Time!
